requirement: The Habeas crate MUST have a Cargo integration test that invokes `habeas::validate()` against its own project, so its own requirements and evidence are checked recursively by `cargo test`.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation. The Habeas crate must have a Cargo integration test that calls `habeas::validate()` on its own project, so `cargo test` checks it recursively.

`tests/habeas.rs#fn[habeas]` is marked `{test}` for `requirements.integration.self_test`. It is a `#[test]` function in the `tests/` directory, so Cargo builds it as an integration test. It calls `habeas::validate()` directly.

The test has no assertion of its own. That is adequate here because `src/lib.rs#fn[validate]` finds the project root, which is the nearest ancestor containing both `Cargo.toml` and `book.toml`. It runs `validate_repository` on that root and panics with all errors if the report contains any. A validation failure in the project therefore fails the test. Nothing else the text states needs a test. The root is found from the current directory, which is the crate when `cargo test` runs.
